title: Flame of the Rising Phoenix
summary: A heretical Dharma that seeks lost humanity.

claims.text: Rising Phoenixes follow the teachings of Kataragama, though they argue over what those words mean, and seek their own humanity rather than exalting themselves as so many Kuei-jin do.
They try to put right the mistakes of their past; outsiders know the Dharma mostly through stereotypes.
Few great bodhisattvas of the Phoenix still walk the world.

title: Tempest of the Inward Focus
summary: A heretical Dharma that rejects the courts' rules.

claims.text: Its followers call the Great Principle and the rules of the court mistresses comforting lies that only prop up the superstitions of mortal life.
They hold that no part of the self may outweigh another, so they pursue lust and celebration, peace and violence, pain and pleasure alike to keep the scales level.

title: The Face of the Gods
summary: A heretical Dharma that seeks to be divine.

claims.text: Where most Kuei-jin simulate life to learn its lessons, this Dharma seeks to experience divinity, and holds that spending Chi works miracles.
Its two sects agree that displays of power redeem the half-living bodies Heaven forced on them.
Raising new vampires falls to individuals of suitable age, and some natural gurus draw more disciples than others; initiates spend their first five years under instruction.

title: Spirit of the Living Earth
summary: A Japanese heretical Dharma that hopes to become kami.

claims.text: Followers hope to shed their dead flesh and become kami, since the kami each know a piece of how a soul can survive without a body and without turning into a goryo.
They perform rites every night, for ancestors, for the spirits of their resting places or for the kami guarding local dragon lines, and each rite needs preparation, tools and chosen offerings.

title: The Scorpion Eaters
summary: Kuei-jin who feed on tainted Chi and give rein to their P'o.

claims.text: The Scorpion Eaters scorn ethics and enlightenment as childish relics of the ancestors and give their P'o free rein.
Tainted Chi marks their bodies, and they wear the signs of Demon Shintai as badges of power.
They live on the edges of Kuei-jin society, taking over any Dragon Nest that becomes tainted and gathering at Broken Mirrors and other places that misery has warped.
